summary: GRAVEYARD discovery pass completed the Chief-selected 12-company batch while keeping the due discovery mesh current. Machine gating sources are fresh, FINRA OTCE was independently checked at the event layer rather than treating partition freshness as row-level ingestion, and no same-cycle discovery justifies automatic membership or score changes. The strongest cross-batch weak signal remains increasing dependence on the same AI-infrastructure capital cycle plus power, interconnect, export-control and qualification bottlenecks; those dependencies should be treated as correlated origins rather than twelve independent confirmations.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Record backlog plus post-quarter launch wins, acquisitions and the announced Iridium transaction expand Rocket Lab from launch toward vertically integrated space infrastructure. The hidden signal is not merely backlog growth but increasing dependence on integration, regulatory approvals and capital allocation across multiple acquired capabilities.
contradictions: More vertical integration increases strategic optionality but also multiplies integration and execution dependencies before Neutron is proven.
unknowns: Current government-award contribution to new backlog, transaction-close dependencies, and exact Neutron qualification schedule.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Acquisition integration or Neutron slips absorb capital without producing repeatable launch/space-systems economics.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: FY2026 end-customer concentration remains an unusually strong weak-signal amplifier: three end-customer profiles accounted for 32%, 33% and 19% of revenue. Any architecture shift at one hyperscaler can propagate rapidly through reported growth.
contradictions: Rapid customer/program expansion may broaden the base, but contracting-entity diversification is not the same as independent end-customer diversification.
unknowns: Current quarter program count, customer-specific contract duration and whether newer optical/DSP wins materially reduce concentration.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Subsequent filings show durable multi-customer diversification without margin erosion.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q2 revenue reached $392.4M with very high gross profitability while Scorpio ramps. The discovery-relevant question is whether Astera is becoming a broader rack-scale connectivity platform or remains tied to a small number of platform ramps.
contradictions: Strong financial scaling supports platform validation, but rapid product-family concentration can hide end-customer dependence.
unknowns: True end-customer map for Scorpio deployments and breadth of independent production programs.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Future filings show Scorpio or one platform dominates revenue without broadening customer adoption.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: The latest 10-Q still shows concentrated customers, while BIS policy keeps China advanced-compute access conditional and license-driven. This is a live policy/market-structure signal because restrictions can both remove addressable market and accelerate substitute ecosystems.
contradictions: Global demand remains extraordinary even while China data-center access is constrained.
unknowns: Durable China re-entry economics and rate at which custom accelerators erode incremental hyperscaler wallet share.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Policy access normalizes without meaningful competitive-share leakage and customer concentration declines materially.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q2 Data Center revenue more than doubled and represented 58% of company revenue, while Instinct remains exposed to the same export-license regime as advanced competing accelerators. The weak signal is a rapidly increasing company-level dependence on AI accelerator execution.
contradictions: Broader CPU leadership diversifies AMD, but the growth narrative is increasingly tied to Data Center and Instinct scaling.
unknowns: Repeat-order breadth across independent Instinct customers and normalized accelerator economics.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Instinct deployments fail to broaden beyond a narrow set of customers or software adoption stalls.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Q3 AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7B and management guided to $21.7B for Q4. This scale turns custom accelerators/networking from a catalyst into a dominant regime exposure; prior filing evidence also shows concentrated channel/end-customer economics.
contradictions: Very high free cash flow and VMware diversification buffer financing risk, but they do not remove hyperscaler concentration.
unknowns: Number and relative size of custom accelerator customers and durability of financed AI-infrastructure buildouts.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Custom-program growth broadens across many independent buyers while concentration metrics fall.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: Advanced nodes were 77% of Q2 wafer revenue and 2nm already contributed 3%, confirming accelerated leading-edge dependence. The overlooked discovery question is whether geographic diversification becomes a second bottleneck through duplicated capex, talent and yield learning.
contradictions: Technology leadership strengthens the bottleneck thesis while overseas replication can structurally dilute economics.
unknowns: Normalized margin/capex burden of overseas leading-edge fabs and customer willingness to pay resilience premiums.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Overseas fabs achieve Taiwan-like yields/economics quickly enough that geographic resilience ceases to be a material constraint.

perCompanyCoverage.signal: ASML entered 2026 with €38.8B backlog and guided for growth, but it explicitly expected China sales to decline significantly versus 2024-25. Export policy therefore remains a live demand-routing signal, not merely a historical risk factor.
contradictions: EUV/High-NA scarcity supports pricing power while geographic policy can alter shipment timing and mix independent of technical demand.
unknowns: Current China mix and High-NA utilization economics at customer production scale.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: China decline is fully absorbed by non-China demand with no material utilization, margin or order volatility.

signal: Top-five customers represented about 57% of FY2026 revenue, Arm China about 16%, and SoftBank-linked arrangements remain material. The weak signal is ecosystem power concentration beneath an asset-light licensing model.
contradictions: Asset-light royalties create operating leverage, but concentration and related-party dependence can transmit external shocks quickly.
unknowns: Independent data-center royalty contribution and pace of RISC-V substitution in new designs.
falsifier: Customer concentration declines while data-center royalty growth broadens across independent licensees.

signal: Q3 revenue rose to $41.46B, cloud-memory gross margin reached 83%, and management guided Q4 gross margin near 86%. Such extraordinary memory economics are themselves a regime-change signal that requires testing for scarcity durability versus eventual supply response.
contradictions: Strategic customer agreements increase visibility while record profitability can attract aggressive industry capacity.
unknowns: Contract floors/take-or-pay protection and competitor HBM4 yield/capacity trajectories.
falsifier: Supply expansion causes fast HBM/DRAM pricing normalization despite strategic agreements.

ready_for_chief.signal: Q2 became Arista's first $3B revenue quarter and new 1.6 Tbps liquid-cooled AI fabrics expand its addressable role. The hidden signal is whether Ethernet consolidates as the common AI fabric or remains vulnerable to proprietary/custom architectures at the largest buyers.
contradictions: Broad-based growth and platform expansion support adoption, but cloud-titan concentration can make architecture decisions discontinuous.
unknowns: Current top-customer share and independent-buyer adoption of 1.6T platforms.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Large customers increasingly internalize switching/network stacks or alternative fabrics gain material scale-out share.

ready_for_chief.signal: Vertiv's filing explicitly warns that customer orders can be unpredictable/cancelled and backlog may not convert. This matters because the AI power/cooling scarcity narrative can produce double-ordering or schedule deferrals when utility/interconnection constraints delay data-center builds.
contradictions: Strong order growth is consistent with real scarcity, while cancellation and project-timing risk prevent backlog from being treated as cash-like demand.
unknowns: Backlog aging, cancellation terms and current hyperscale/colocation customer concentration.
ready_for_chief.falsifier: Backlog converts on schedule with low cancellation and broad customer diversification despite grid delays.

materialFindings.finding: Automated gating mesh is current at 2026-09-14T06:10Z with 4/4 required sources healthy; FINRA is only partition-freshness at the automated layer, so event-layer corroboration was checked separately rather than overstated.

FINRA OTCE showed zero Daily List events for Saturday 2026-09-12; this is useful corroboration but does not create a false Monday 2026-09-14 event claim before the next business-day publication window.

BIS semiconductor-export rules remain live and current through the September 11, 2026 EAR publication state; no fresh same-cycle rule was found that supersedes the January 2026 case-by-case H200/MI325X policy.

Across the active batch, AI-capex demand, advanced-node capacity, memory scarcity, high-speed interconnect and data-center power are correlated causal origins. Repeated corporate revenue growth should not be counted as independent evidence of twelve unrelated theses.

contradictions: Rapid growth across CRDO, ALAB, NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TSM, MU, ANET and VRT is partly common-origin AI infrastructure spending; cross-company repetition can inflate perceived independent confirmation.
Automated FINRA health is fresh but not row-level event acquisition; the system correctly distinguishes capability from reachability and must continue doing so.
unknowns: Monday 2026-09-14 FINRA Daily List event rows are not yet observable at this graveyard-hour review; no event claim is inferred from the fresh partition alone.
No same-cycle primary evidence established a new outside-250 company strong enough for admission consideration without further underwriting.
Several batch companies still lack normalized end-customer concentration on a comparable basis.

peerRequests.request: Keep FINRA eventDataAvailable=false explicit until actual row-level acquisition exists; do not promote partition freshness into event coverage.
Normalize CRDO/ALAB/ANET end-customer concentration and RKLB/VRT backlog quality before batch promotion.
Model AI-capex/power/interconnect as common-origin dependencies so repeated company growth does not inflate independent causal confidence.

accuracyDebates.reason: Multiple batch companies are reporting the same underlying AI infrastructure buildout through different products; Earth should preserve this as one macro origin with company-specific transmission paths.
Partition freshness and event-level acquisition remain distinct and current tooling truth supports keeping that distinction explicit.
